policy_title: Strengthen workers' rights and trade union powers
stated: Repeal current anti-union legislation, replace it with a Charter of Workers’ Rights, restore the right to strike, and provide full employment rights from day one for all workers, including gig economy workers and those on zero-hours contracts.

source.quote: Elected Greens would campaign to: • Repeal current anti-union legislation and replace this with a positive Charter of Workers’ Rights. • Deliver equal rights for all workers currently excluded from protections, including ‘gig economy’ workers and those on ‘zero hours’ contracts. We will legislate for workers to have full employment rights from day one of their employment. We will restore the right to strike, remove arbitrary ballot thresholds and outdated requirements for postal ballots for strike action, and overturn bans on secondary picketing and industrial action for political objectives.

bearing_set.reason: Full employment rights from day one, covering gig and zero-hours workers, directly affects pay levels, job security, conditions, and in-work protections — the core of good work and fair pay.

Restoring the right to strike and repealing anti-union legislation directly affect civil liberties recognised under ECHR Article 11 (freedom of association and collective action); a Charter of Workers' Rights constitutes a formal legal-rights framework.
Repealing anti-union legislation and restoring the right to strike removes existing state-imposed restrictions on collective action, directly improving this liberty indicator.

A reform of this scale — extending full employment rights and union powers across all workers — plausibly affects business investment decisions, labour-market flexibility, and firm dynamism; the aggregate prosperity effect (positive or negative) is real and contested.

Extending employment rights to precarious and low-paid workers (gig economy, zero-hours) and restoring collective bargaining would plausibly narrow the income-protection gap between high and low earners.

membership_note: Four fundamentals: O4 is the primary designed-for outcome; O10 is the civil-liberty gain from removing strike restrictions; O13 captures the contested macroeconomic spillover on investment and dynamism; O14 reflects the distributional effect on the income gap via collective bargaining and extension of rights to precarious workers.
